Describe an AMD curve and its stored partitions

Source: R/diagnose_amd.R
diagnose_amd.Rd

Summarise the primary curve, memberships and hard assignments without fitting new models, selecting a number of groups or changing the input. The selected fits must be those saved by compute_amd_curve().

Usage

diagnose_amd(object, ambiguity_gap = 0.1)

Arguments

object

An amd_curve with a primary curve and a selected fit for every evaluated candidate. Legacy 0.1.0 objects are not sufficient.

ambiguity_gap

A number in [0, 1]. An observation is counted as ambiguous when its largest membership minus its second-largest membership is strictly less than this value. The default, 0.1, is a descriptive convention, not a validated universal decision threshold.

Value

An object of class amd_diagnostics with:

candidates

One row per evaluated c, describing curve neighbours, winning memberships, normalised membership entropy, top-two gaps and hard and soft group-size balance. Boundary local maxima are NA, since one neighbour is missing. A local maximum here means strictly greater than both evaluated neighbours; plateaus are not classified as peaks.

groups

One row per membership column at each c. Hard sizes use the stored winning assignment. Soft masses are sums of memberships, not of memberships raised to the fuzziness parameter. Summaries within a hard group are NA when that group is empty.

transitions

ARI, geometric-mean normalised mutual information (NMI) and directional fragmentation between successive evaluated candidates. Fragmentation is the fraction outside each group's most frequent group in the other partition. from_fragmentation describes splitting of source groups; to_fragmentation describes mixing of source groups in destination groups. These are descriptive overlaps, not evidence of physical splitting, merging or biological stability.

curve_summary

Numerical maximum, exact ties, boundary status and the evaluated range. These do not constitute a scientific choice of K.

dictionary

Definitions and scales for every table column.

unavailable

Diagnostics not computed by this operation and why.

complete_rows, omitted_rows

The original observation row map.

settings

Diagnostic conventions and provenance.

Details

Normalised observation entropy is -sum(u * log(u)) / log(c), with 0 * log(0) interpreted as zero. Size entropy applies the same formula to group fractions. Quantiles use stats::quantile() with type = 8. Exact top-membership ties are reported separately and the stored assignment is retained; no new tie-breaking or random-number generation takes place.

Transitions compare the same observations, not the numerical group labels. ARI and NMI are invariant to relabelling. Identical single-group partitions have ARI and NMI one even if their occupied membership columns differ. NMI is zero when only one of the partitions has a single occupied group.

This function uses memberships and assignments only. It does not calculate sample-to-sample distances, silhouette, geometric compactness, density, connectivity or resampling stability, and does not require the original data. It does not impute missing descriptive values or call a supervised reader. Its working arrays grow linearly with the number of observations per candidate, plus contingency tables between occupied groups; it does not construct an observation-by-observation distance matrix.

See also

compute_amd_curve(), assign_configurations(), amd_score()

Examples

set.seed(42)
X <- rbind(matrix(rnorm(40, -2), ncol = 2),
           matrix(rnorm(40, 2), ncol = 2))
curve <- compute_amd_curve(X, its = 2, nin = 2, nsp = 3,
                           seeds = 1:4, iter_max = 1000, verbose = FALSE)
diagnostics <- diagnose_amd(curve)
diagnostics$candidates
#>   c       amd mean_winning_membership q10_winning_membership
#> 1 2 0.4353950               0.9353950              0.8357168
#> 2 3 0.5243304               0.8576638              0.6019939
#>   median_winning_membership mean_membership_entropy q90_membership_entropy
#> 1                 0.9561074               0.2826285              0.6416417
#> 2                 0.8999393               0.3701649              0.7165261
#>   mean_top_two_gap q10_top_two_gap ambiguous_fraction tied_winner_fraction
#> 1        0.8707900       0.6714337              0.025                    0
#> 2        0.7443122       0.2977249              0.025                    0
#>   minimum_hard_fraction maximum_hard_fraction hard_size_entropy
#> 1                  0.50                 0.500         1.0000000
#> 2                  0.25                 0.475         0.9604876
#>   empty_hard_groups minimum_soft_fraction maximum_soft_fraction
#> 1                 0             0.4892867             0.5107133
#> 2                 0             0.2642398             0.4608214
#>   soft_size_entropy delta_previous   drop_next at_boundary local_maximum
#> 1         0.9996688             NA -0.08893545        TRUE            NA
#> 2         0.9682197     0.08893545          NA        TRUE            NA
#>   at_numerical_maximum
#> 1                FALSE
#> 2                 TRUE
diagnostics$transitions
#>   from_c to_c c_step amd_change       ari       nmi from_fragmentation
#> 1      2    3      1 0.08893545 0.6666225 0.7125278              0.275
#>   to_fragmentation
#> 1            0.025
# Inspect the curve and diagnostics before making an explicit choice.
assigned <- assign_configurations(curve, c = 2)
